## 6. Australia — AI News
- 2026-04-16 | [Generative Artificial Intelligence Practice Note (GPN-AI)](https://www.fedcourt.gov.au/law-and-practice/practice-documents/notice-to-profession/16-april-2026): The Federal Court of Australia issued a new practice note requiring verification of authorities and facts, and disclosure where generative AI use could affect pleadings, evidence, or admissibility.
  Why it matters: This is a direct Australian governance action that changes how AI can be used in federal litigation.

## 7. AI Workflows & Tactics
2026-04-16 | [Vibe Coding Gets an Upgrade](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rNDaRO68JEc)

Summary: The actionable workflow is multi-session agent orchestration for software work: run parallel AI coding sessions against the same repo, each with terminal access and narrow task ownership, then use routines/triggers to automate recurring actions.

Tools/models: Multi-session developer interfaces, integrated terminals, workspace customization, and Claude Code routines/trigger-based automation.

Setup:
1. Open the target repo in an agentic coding tool that supports multiple sessions and terminal access.
2. Split work into bounded lanes such as implementation, tests, debugging, and docs.
3. Assign one session per lane with a narrow prompt and clear file ownership.
4. Add routines or triggers so recurring events kick off background actions automatically.
5. Merge outputs back through a primary review session before committing changes.

Availability: Available now, per the supplied video summary.

Why it matters: This is a practical shift from single-threaded prompting to orchestrated parallel execution, which can reduce developer wait time and make automation repeatable.
